causes: Never trained, trained in a language not understood, new worker (< 30 days), unfamiliar equipment
Incentives for speed, no consequence for shortcuts, supervisors tolerating violations
Fatigue, heat, illness, intoxication, poor vision/hearing, stress
Right tool unavailable, poor lighting, bad access, defective equipment, poor design
No method statement, impractical procedure, no permit control, no pre-task briefing, low supervisor presence
No risk assessment, no inspection/maintenance programme, poor contractor control, lessons not learned, resources not provided
models: For every serious injury there are many minor injuries, more near misses and far more unsafe acts/conditions; control the base to prevent the top
Accidents happen when holes in multiple layers of defence line up; latent conditions (management) and active failures (acts) combine
Lack of control → basic causes (personal/job factors) → immediate causes (substandard acts/conditions) → incident → loss
Eliminate → substitute → engineering → administrative → PPE; conditions are usually fixed by engineering, acts by training, supervision and design that makes the safe way the easy way
Antecedents trigger behaviour; consequences (soon, certain, positive) sustain it; observe, give feedback, remove barriers, recognise safe behaviour
